summary: Defines a PPP Link Control Protocol option that lets peers negotiate the language and character set used in messages. It updates RFC 1570, RFC 1994 and RFC 2284. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This PPP option lets two peers agree on the language and character set for messages intended for people. If they do not agree to use the option, the sender uses the specified defaults.

questions: what is the ppp lcp internationalization option
what is the default charset for ppp messages
subtitle: A PPP LCP option for negotiating the language and character set of human-readable messages.

tldr.problem: PPP's LCP and authentication packets can contain text for people, so peers need a way to agree on the text's language and character set.
tldr.mechanism: The Internationalization option carries a four-octet MIBenum character-set identifier and an ASCII language tag.
tldr.outcome: If a peer rejects the option, the sender must use the default language and character set. RFC 2484 updates RFCs 1570, 1994 and 2284.

today: RFC 2484 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 1570, RFC 1994 and RFC 2284. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Option Is Needed
sections.content:
The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) defines the Link Control Protocol (LCP), which can negotiate authentication before network-layer protocols use the link. LCP and authentication packets may contain human-readable text.

This RFC defines an LCP configuration option to negotiate the language and character set for that text. The option may be negotiated independently in each direction, and an implementation should send only one instance for its preferred language and character set.
sections.plainLanguage: Some PPP messages contain text for people to read. The option lets peers say which language and character set to use for that text.

sections.title: Option Type and Defaults
sections.content:
The Internationalization option uses LCP option type 28. If the peer rejects it, the sender must use the default language and character set for all human-readable messages sent to that peer.

The option's character-set field identifies a registered character set. Its default is UTF-8, identified by MIBenum value 106. Its default language tag is i-default.
sections.plainLanguage: The option has type 28. If the peer does not accept it, the sender uses UTF-8 and the default language tag i-default.

sections.title: Fields in the Option
sections.content:
The option contains a type field, a length field, a four-octet MIBenum field and a Language-Tag field. The total length must be at least 7. MIBenum must identify a character set in the IANA registry.

The Language-Tag is an ASCII string defined by RFC 1766. Tags are case-insensitive in principle, but implementations should send them in lowercase because capitalization has no meaning.
sections.plainLanguage: The option includes a number for the character set and a text tag for the language. Language tags do not distinguish uppercase from lowercase, so implementations should send lowercase tags.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC warns that an attacker might manipulate the option so that displayable messages become unintelligible to the reader. It provides no further security mechanism.
sections.plainLanguage: An attacker could change the negotiated settings so that people cannot read messages sent to them.
